description: Live, on-device text recognition: Apple Vision on iOS, ML Kit on Android. The text-scanning sibling to mobile_scanner.
rules: text_sight does live and one-shot on-device text recognition via each platform native engine, Apple Vision on iOS (a system framework, so iOS links zero third-party ML libraries: no GoogleMLKit) and ML Kit on Android. No recognition lib in your pubspec.
Import only the barrel 'package:text_sight/text_sight.dart'. Never import from lib/src/ directly.

Live recognition: create a TextSightController, render a TextSightView, then call controller.start() once camera permission is granted (the view does NOT auto-start). Read results via onResult or controller.captures. Boxes are normalized [0,1], top-left.

One-shot recognition (no camera, session, or permission): await TextSight.recognizeImage(bytes) or TextSight.recognizePath(path). Both take an optional TextSightOptions, which defaults to RecognitionLevel.accurate.

Reconfigure a running session through the controller's update* methods (updateRegionOfInterest, updateRecognitionLevel, updateLanguages, updateTorchEnabled), each an async command returning Future<void>, not a set* method or setter.

Platforms: iOS 15.0+ (Vision uses the modern RecognizeTextRequest on 18+ and the legacy VNRecognizeTextRequest on 15-17, and iOS 15-16 don't follow live device rotation), Android API 24+ (ML Kit Latin). recognitionLevel/languages apply on iOS only, Android Latin ignores them. Region-of-interest is a normalized Rect. iOS restricts Vision to it. Android crops one-shot, live keeps centred lines.

RecognizedLine.confidence is double? in [0,1]. null means the engine supplied none (never synthesized), and the scales are not comparable across platforms, nor across iOS versions (modern RecognizeTextRequest is coarse and often 1.0, legacy VNRecognizeTextRequest is graded).

Camera permission ships with the package, so no permission_handler is needed: controller.checkCameraPermission() reads the status without prompting, controller.requestCameraPermission() drives the system prompt, and both resolve to a CameraPermissionStatus.

Model readiness lives on TextSightModel, shared by both drivers. On Android the default unbundled ML Kit model is fetched from Google Play Services and requests made before it arrives yield no results, so call TextSightModel.ensureReady() when the user enters an OCR feature and watch the TextSightModel.readiness stream of TextSightReadinessState for download progress. On iOS Vision is a system framework, so it is already ready.
